definition: A RESTful, stateless web service for the PI System. Its root URL is https://<server>/piwebapi and its built-in help is at /piwebapi/help. It is built on AF SDK and exposes a subset of it, so any platform that can make HTTP requests can read and write PI and AF data.
A persistent, URL-safe identifier that PI Web API uses to address an object (PI point, element, attribute and so on) in URLs. WebIDs can be stored by client applications.

The open WebID format introduced in PI Web API 2017 R2. WebID 1.0 was opaque; WebID 2.0 follows an open specification so clients can build and decode WebIDs themselves. Character 1 is the type letter, character 2 the version, characters 3-4 the object-type marker, then Base64url-encoded IDs and/or path.
The default WebID 2.0 type (type letter F). It encodes both the object IDs and the path, so it is the longest form and the most resilient.
A WebID 2.0 type (type letter I) that encodes only the object IDs. It survives moves and renames but becomes invalid when the object is deleted.
A WebID 2.0 type (type letter P) that encodes only the object's path, so a client can build it without a lookup. It breaks when the object is renamed and always points to whatever is at that path.
PI Web API query parameter that chooses which WebID type the response uses, for example ?webIdType=PathOnly or webidtype=idonly.
In PI Web API, the time series of a PI point or an AF attribute, addressed as /streams/{webId}. Stream endpoints include value, end, recorded, interpolated, plot, summary and channel.
A set of streams read or written in one PI Web API call: either all attributes of an element (/streamsets/{webId}/...) or an ad hoc list of WebIDs passed as a repeated webId query parameter.
PI Web API query parameter that trims a response to the listed fields, given as semicolon-separated dotted paths such as Items.Timestamp;Items.Value.
The object in each PI Web API response that holds URLs to related resources, so a client can navigate the API. The root response Links include Self, AssetServers, DataServers, Omf, Search and System.

The HTTP header that PI Web API's CSRF (cross-site request forgery) defence requires on POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE requests. Any value works; samples use XmlHttpRequest. GET requests are not affected.

A browser mechanism that lets a web page from another origin call a service. PI Web API configures it with the attributes CorsOrigins, CorsMethods, CorsHeaders, CorsExposedHeaders and CorsSupportsCredentials.
The tool that manages PI Web API installation-level settings: Telemetry, Configuration Store, Authentication, AIM Registration, Listen Port, Certificate, API Service and OMF Servers.
Boolean PI Web API configuration attribute that, when set, makes the service read-only.

AVEVA's OpenID Connect identity provider, used for claims-based authentication in the PI System. It runs as a Windows service, is part of Platform Common Services, uses Windows AD by default and can federate one more identity provider (AVEVA Connect, recommended, or Azure AD).

An authentication layer on top of OAuth 2.0. PI Web API accepts it as Bearer authentication; its discovery document is fetched from /.well-known/openid-configuration. Bearer and Kerberos cannot be enabled together on PI Web API.
A model with StatusCode (integer) and Errors (list of strings) that appears as a WebException property on objects returned inside batch and bulk PI Web API responses.

One time-series item in a PI Web API response, with Timestamp, Value, UnitsAbbreviation and the flags Good, Questionable, Substituted and Annotated. Digital states come back as an object with Name and Value.

The PI Web API Search controller (for example /search/query?q=...), backed by index files built by the PI Web API Crawler. It is an optional feature, and results depend on the crawler having indexed the objects.
A separate, optional service that crawls AF databases to build the index files used by Indexed Search. PI Vision 2020 no longer uses it.

Token syntax used by AF SDK search classes (AFElementSearch, AFEventFrameSearch, AFAttributeSearch) and passed through by PI Web API search query methods, for example Name:=*b* AND Template:=PumpTemplate or Template:'Pump' Name:'P*'.
A WebSocket subscription in PI Web API that pushes new values for a stream or stream set over a persistent connection. Secure channel URLs start with wss:// instead of https://.
A protocol for a persistent two-way connection over which a server can push messages. PI Web API channels use it.

PI Web API's HTTP-only (non-WebSocket) way to get new data. A client registers with POST /streams/{webId}/updates, receives a marker, then polls GET /streams/updates/{marker}; results are queued server-side so the client gets only new data. It appeared as a CTP around PI Web API 2018 SP1.
An opaque token returned by Stream Updates that marks the position from which to fetch the next updates. Each response includes the next marker (LatestMarker) to send in the following request.

The PI Web API controller that runs many sub-requests in one HTTP POST to /batch. Each named sub-request has Method and Resource and optionally Content, Headers, ParentIds, Parameters and RequestTemplate. GET is not supported on /batch.

Batch property listing the sub-requests that must complete first. It is used with Parameters: JSONPath expressions such as $.1.Content.WebId whose results fill {0}, {1} placeholders in the child's Resource.
Batch property holding a parameterised Resource so one sub-request can be repeated over many parameter values, for example every WebID returned by a parent request.
verifyNote: The exact RequestTemplate JSON shape and expansion behaviour were partly inferred; check against the PI Web API Batch documentation.

definition: A path syntax for picking values out of JSON. PI Web API batch supports $ (root), dot notation ($.C.D), index ($.B[0].Val) and wildcard ($.B[*].Val).

The PI Web API endpoint, added in the 2019 release, that accepts OSIsoft Message Format messages POSTed to {piwebapi}/omf. The OMF option must be selected when installing PI Web API for it to be available.

OMF (OSIsoft Message Format) sends three kinds of JSON message, chosen with the messagetype header: type (the schema), container (a stream of one type) and data (values). They must be sent in that order, and a type cannot be changed once defined.

AF SDK collection of the AF servers known to the client. Each item is a PISystem (one AF server), reached with systems["name"] or systems.DefaultPISystem; its Databases collection holds the AF databases.
AF SDK collection of PI Data Archives known to the client. Each item is a PIServer, for example new PIServers().DefaultPIServer, used to find and create PI points.

AF SDK client-side cache of attribute values. You Add an attribute list, set CacheTimeSpan, call UpdateData() and Subscribe an observer; internally it uses a data pipe to receive updates from the server.
AF SDK mechanism to subscribe to new events for attributes. Each AFDataPipeEvent carries a Value (an AFValue) and an Action. For PI-point attributes it reads using a TimeSeries pipe.

AF SDK sign-up mechanism for update events on PI points. You create it with a type (Snapshot, Archive or TimeSeries), AddSignups, poll GetUpdateEvents, then Close and Dispose it. Choosing the pipe type is only possible on PIDataPipe.
AF SDK enumeration that controls how values at the edges of a time range are returned by recorded-value calls. Samples use Inside and Interpolated.
AF SDK enumeration that controls write behaviour in UpdateValue and UpdateValues, for example Insert or Remove.
AF SDK setting for bulk list calls on PIPointList or AFAttributeList, for example new PIPagingConfiguration(PIPageType.TagCount, 100), so a large request is sent in pages.
AF SDK call that commits pending AF object changes to the AF server, for example database.CheckIn(). Samples guard it with if (database.IsDirty). Without it, changes stay local and uncommitted.

An AFSearch clause that filters on a related object, added in AF SDK 2.9.5. Example: Element:{Name:'Boiler*'} Name:'Feed Rate' finds Feed Rate attributes on elements named Boiler*. A nested query cannot contain its own nested query.

The package of PI SQL drivers (OLE DB, ODBC v3 and a pure-Java JDBC driver) that send SQL to PI SQL Data Access Server. Version 2018 had only OLE DB; 2018 R2 added ODBC and JDBC and removed the AF SDK dependency.

The Real-Time Query Processor hosted by PI SQL Data Access Server. Each connection targets one AF database, exposed as the Master catalog with tables such as Master.Element.Element and Master.EventFrame.EventFrame.

The only built-in RTQP catalog. Its tables include Master.Element.Element, Master.Element.Attribute (with ValueTimeStamp and Value for the current value) and Master.EventFrame.EventFrame. There is no separate snapshot table.
RTQP functions such as [Master].[Element].[GetSummary] and GetSampledValues that take an element template name plus attribute names and return a table. They are invoked with CROSS APPLY.
Middleware that PI SQL clients connect to over net.tcp or HTTPS. It hosts the RTQP engine (and an Integrator Framework variant) and is required by the PI JDBC driver.
OLE DB provider for PI Data Archive point data with read/write (CRUD) access, not AF. Its catalogs are piarchive (archive tables), pipoint (point configuration), pids (digital states) and piuser.
OLE DB provider with read-only access to AF assets, event frames and AF attribute data. Queries written for it can be migrated to the RTQP engine.

Java database driver (JDBC 4.0 to 4.2) that works over HTTPS only and needs PI SQL Data Access Server. Class com.osisoft.jdbc.Driver, URL form jdbc:pisql://<das_node>/Data Source=<pi_server>; Integrated Security=SSPI;.
ODBC v3 driver for PI data over net.tcp or HTTPS, now part of PI SQL Client. Connection string example: DRIVER=PI SQL Client;Integrated Security=SSPI;AF Server=PISRV01;AF Database=WindFarm.
PI OLEDB Provider table of archived (compressed) events with their real timestamps. It stores values as variants, so some clients need cast(value as Float32).
PI OLEDB Provider table of interpolated values at a timestep; the manual calls it the newer, recommended version of piinterp. The timestep defaults to 1 hour, aligned to the query time.
Query tool for PI SQL. The Lite edition connects to RTQP and PI OLEDB Enterprise and offers model browsing, a Query Compendium and SQL generation for table-valued-function templates.

Product that reads data from PI Asset Framework, shapes it into views and writes it to third-party platforms called targets. Standard Edition does scheduled bulk updates; Advanced Edition is a superset that adds streaming views.

A reusable, template-based pattern of AF elements and attributes, built in the Shape Builder, that defines a view's structure. Shape elements are matched by template and can be filtered by asset name or template.
PI Integrator view based on elements and element templates; its columns come from asset attributes, sampled between a start and end time at an interval.
PI Integrator view based on event frames and event frame templates; its columns come from event frame attributes.
PI Integrator view for targets that support streaming, such as Apache Kafka, Azure Event Hub and Azure IoT Hub. Only Advanced Edition supports it.
A third-party platform that PI Integrator writes view data to, such as Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle, Azure SQL Database, Apache Kafka, Amazon S3 or Google BigQuery.
The unit PI Integrator is licensed by: a unique PI tag used in a view, counted once across views. Static attributes do not consume streams, and removing a view does not free its streams.
PI Integrator target that exposes a view for ODBC/SQL query. It is for development and test only and is deprecated because of a security vulnerability; use a SQL Server target when one is available.

Open-source, MIT-licensed Python connector to the PI System and PI AF that works through the AF SDK. Recorded values come back as a decorated pandas Series. Install with conda install PIconnect or pip install PIconnect.

term: PowerShell Tools for the PI System
definition: PowerShell module (OSIsoft.PowerShell) that ships with PI System Management Tools 2015 and later. Cmdlets include Connect-PIDataArchive, Get-PIPoint, Get-PIValue, Add-PIValue and Start-PIBackup.
PowerShell Tools cmdlet that opens a connection object to a PI Data Archive, for example $con = Connect-PIDataArchive -PIDataArchiveMachineName PISRV01. Other cmdlets take it through -Connection.
Python package that adds HTTPKerberosAuth to the requests library for Kerberos (Negotiate) authentication. AVEVA's PI Web API samples use it with mutual_authentication='REQUIRED'.

AVEVA's cloud data service, formerly AVEVA Data Hub and before that OSIsoft Cloud Services. It is powered by the Sequential Data Store and offers REST APIs under {resource}/api/{version}/Tenants/{tenantId}/Namespaces/{namespaceId}.
verifyNote: The product name timeline (OSIsoft Cloud Services to AVEVA Data Hub to CONNECT data services) and its dates are not confirmed by a dated source.

definition: The storage engine of CONNECT data services for types, streams and indexed data.

The schema of a stream's events in the Sequential Data Store. It is defined with SdsTypeCode values (such as Object, Double, DateTime) and a property flagged IsKey as the index; time series use a DateTime key.
A sequence of events of one SdsType in the Sequential Data Store, managed through /Streams and read through /Streams/{id}/Data.
The top-level CONNECT data services account container. Its ID appears in every REST path and in client-credentials sign-in.
A logical container within a tenant that isolates types, streams and data views.

A server-side definition that queries streams and returns aligned interpolated or stored tabular data through /dataviews/{id}/data/interpolated and /data/stored. Paging follows links in the HTTP Link header.
A cross-tenant sharing space for streams. When a CommunityId is set in AVEVA's samples, the namespace ID is ignored.

OAuth 2.0 machine-to-machine sign-in used by services calling CONNECT data services: tenant ID, client ID and client secret are exchanged at the token endpoint for an access token. It gives no refresh token.

OAuth 2.0 sign-in flow for single-page and native apps calling CONNECT data services, with silent refresh and no refresh token. The Hybrid flow, for thick apps with a server component, gives both access and refresh tokens.
Paging token in Sequential Data Store window reads. The client repeats the request with the token until it comes back null; ignoring it means only the first page is read.
Optional CONNECT data services request header (verbose or non-verbose) that controls whether default-valued fields are returned in data responses.
